name: Cumbia
notes: Cumbia style pack (Doc 04 template, solo-first). Born on Colombia's Caribbean coast as a TRI-ETHNIC creation — African drums and dance carried by enslaved people, Indigenous gaita flutes and maracas, Spanish dress and melody — courtship danced at night around candles, the woman carrying the flame while the man circles. The candle lore is well-documented tradition; cumbia's second miracle is its travel: no Latin American rhythm is more widely shared — Mexican cumbia (sonidera, Selena's Tejano cumbias), Argentine cumbia, Peruvian chicha, and the modern digital wave all keep the same rolling pulse, making cumbia the continent's common floor. Design truths: the basic shuffle-step is famously easy to enter (the family-party dance everyone's tía teaches) and genuinely solo-trainable; the courtship figures — the circling, the candle arm, the skirt/vueltas — are described and prepped solo; the couple form is 🤝 late; the cumbia pulse lives in this app's Rhythm Trainer.

seasons.finale: Film yourself stepping the cumbia pulse through one full track — the scraper's cha-ka-cha in your feet.
Film the basic back-step shuffle — smooth, grounded, unhurried — one full song each side.
Film the traveling circles and turns — the courtship's orbit, danced solo with the candle arm alive.
Film the basic riding three cumbias from three countries — Colombian folclórica, Mexican sonidera, Peruvian chicha — one step, one continent.
Dance cumbia where it lives: a family party, a Latin night, a quinceañera floor. The tías will find you and approve.

attributes.name: Grounded shuffle L1
attributes.test: 60s of small back-step shuffles, weight fully trading, knees soft, upper body calm

attributes.name: Easy hips L1
attributes.test: 20 relaxed hip sways riding the transfers — a result of the step, never forced

nodes.name: The cumbia pulse — drums and guacharaca
checkpoints: cumbia rolls a relaxed duple pulse: the tambores underneath, the guacharaca scraper's cha-ka-cha on top — it's in this app's Rhythm Trainer
the gaita (Indigenous flute) sings the old melodies; accordion took the lead as vallenato's cousin genres grew
the pulse survives every border crossing — learn it once, dance it from Bogotá to Buenos Aires to LA

nodes.name: One pulse, one continent
checkpoints: Mexican cumbia and sonidera slowed it and made it a street-party institution; Selena's Tejano cumbias carried it into US pop history
Peruvian chicha wired it to surf guitars; Argentine cumbia gave it barrio anthems; the digital wave keeps remixing it
build a five-country playlist and hear the same heartbeat wearing five flags

nodes.name: Three roots, one dance
checkpoints: cumbia was born on Colombia's Caribbean coast from three roots: African drums and dance carried by enslaved people, Indigenous gaita flutes and maracas, and Spanish dress and melody
crediting all three — and the enslaved Africans whose rhythm is its engine — is the ground floor of dancing it
the tradition's image: courtship danced at night, the woman carrying lit candles, the man circling with his sombrero — flame, orbit, and dignity

nodes.name: The courtship's grammar
checkpoints: the folclórica form is an orbit: she holds the center with the candles and the polleras (skirt) speaking; he circles, hat in hand, invited closer or waved off — her choice governs the dance
consent built into the choreography itself: the circling asks, the candle answers
social cumbia keeps the grammar loose — a couple, a circle of friends, or the whole family floor at once

nodes.name: The cumbia back-step shuffle
nodes.anchor: the step every tía teaches in one song
checkpoints: step back small with one foot, replace, and rock — the free foot slides more than lifts; then mirror
grounded and unhurried: cumbia strolls, it never marches
hips sway as a RESULT of honest weight transfers (the bachata pack's law, same floor physics)
keep it going through a whole conversation — party-ready means automatic
mistakes: big backward lunges (the step is a suggestion, not a retreat)
forcing the sway from the waist

nodes.name: The candle arm & the skirt hand
checkpoints: one arm carries the imagined candle — lifted, steady, the flame never spilling; the other holds the skirt (or your shirt hem) sweeping gentle arcs
for the hat role: sombrero (or cap) in hand, carving slow circles as you orbit
learn BOTH roles' arms — the modern floor doesn't assign them by gender, and good dancers own the whole grammar

nodes.name: Vueltas — the traveling orbit
checkpoints: the shuffle travels: circle an imaginary partner clockwise then counter, the basic never breaking
solo turns on the phrase ends — small steps under you, candle arm steady through the spin
the orbit is the courtship's shape; dance it solo until the geometry is yours

nodes.name: Regional accents — one step, many countries
checkpoints: Colombian folclórica keeps the step gliding and the orbit wide; Mexican cumbia tightens it — smaller steps, more hip, the sonidera floor packed shoulder to shoulder
Argentine cumbia leans into the rock-step; chicha adds a springy bounce under the surf guitars
dance all four accents over one week; the step that survives translation is truly yours

nodes.name: The couple form (with a partner)
checkpoints: the orbit with a real center: circling, approaching, invited or waved off — her candle (real or imagined) still governs
social cumbia holds are light and joyful — learned at the party, from the family, in one night
the folclórica staging (polleras, candles, sombreros) lives with folk troupes; the family floor is everyone's

nodes.name: Three countries, one film
checkpoints: film the basic + arms + vueltas riding a Colombian folclórica, a Mexican sonidera, and a Peruvian chicha track
same step, three accents — let each country's pulse change the flavor, not the form
name each track's country on camera; the continental floor deserves its map

nodes.name: The fiesta
checkpoints: dance cumbia where it lives — a family party, a Latin night, a quinceañera, a sonidero street dance
cumbia floors are the least intimidating on earth: three generations, zero judgment, infinite tías
when someone's abuela nods at your shuffle, log this node complete
